avoidWhen: there are a few short sections; showing them all reads faster than folding them
the content is compared across sections; folding forces remembering instead of looking
the sections are alternative views of the same space; that is Tabs
it is a single collapsible surface with no coordination between siblings; that is ExpandableTile
nothing needs to be controlled or listened to from outside: DetailsGroup does it without JavaScript
useWhen: there are several long sections and which stay open is worth coordinating: an FAQ, terms
type=single: opening one closes the previous, so the page does not grow without end
type=multiple: several can stay open at once, and they are still one accordion

avoidWhen: it stands alone, outside an accordion; that is an ExpandableTile
useWhen: it is one section of the accordion; its `value` is how the accordion names it

avoidWhen: it is outside an Accordion.Item; there is nothing for it to open
useWhen: it is the header that opens and closes its section

avoidWhen: it is outside an Accordion.Item; nothing opens it
useWhen: it is the body that folds inside its section

avoidWhen: which one is open has to be controlled from outside, or its changes listened to: that needs Accordion
useWhen: several sections open and close, and letting the browser handle it is enough
only one should stay open: siblings sharing a name already do that on their own

avoidWhen: whether it is open has to be known from outside, or the section has to be disabled: that is Accordion.Item
useWhen: a section that expands and needs no JavaScript at all
it matters that it works before any script loads

avoidWhen: it is outside a Details; there is nothing for it to open
useWhen: it is what the closed state shows and what opens the section

avoidWhen: it is outside a Details; nothing opens it
useWhen: it is what opening reveals

avoidWhen: what is wanted is a numbered legend under a static image, with no leaders or rings: that is a List or a Table
the label has to appear on hover or focus: that is Tooltip, which is floating, ephemeral chrome; this is always drawn
a value next to a control inside a real form needs explaining: that is FormField's `hint`, which is also linked through aria-describedby
the subject has to stay usable: `inert` is all or nothing, so a diagram over a live UI is two things fighting over the same markup
the diagram is boxes and arrows between nodes, not the parts of one thing: this anchors each label to a selector inside the subject, it does not draw a graph
useWhen: the pieces of something already rendered have to be pointed at and named: a component's anatomy, the parts of a composition, an assembly diagram

the marks must not cover it: each part gets a number in one of the four margins of a grid and the subject takes the middle cell, so overlap is not avoided, it cannot be expressed; the names go in an ordered legend below
each number reaches its part by a leader line of one or two segments, straight or at 45 degrees only: the fewest that will do
the drawing recomputes itself when the container resizes, the subject reflows or a font arrives: where a part lands is not a value that can be written when composing
the diagram has to read on a phone: the drawing lives on a canvas, is designed at its own width and shown fitted, with zoom to get close to a part

some parts are areas that contain others (an accordion, one of its items, a panel): `mark: bracket` marks them with a bracket as long as the part, nested outward, instead of a leader that would land on some arbitrary child
the subject is a sample and not a control: `inert` is on, it takes no pointer, focus or keyboard, and leaves the accessibility tree

avoidWhen: it is any cropped image; that is an ImageFrame
useWhen: there is no photo and the person's initials are needed
the avatar identifies someone and needs an accessible name

avoidWhen: it is a content image and not an identity; use ImageFrame
useWhen: a photo identifies a person or an entity
the round crop needs to keep the name as alternative text

avoidWhen: each person needs a visible name, detail or action; use List
useWhen: several identities are shown together in a compact stack
the visible overflow is summarized with a count

avoidWhen: the whole page fits on one screen: there is nowhere to come back from
the point is to skip the chrome at the top and reach the content: that is SkipLink, first in focus order and a real anchor
the destination is a specific section and not the start of the scroller: that is an anchor link in the text, or Toc
focus always has to travel back up too: give it a `target` with the id of something focusable at the start, or see SkipLink
scroll position has to be restored between pages: that is the router's job, not a button's
useWhen: the page is long and someone who scrolled far wants to get back to the top without dragging the scroll by hand
it appears on its own past a scroll threshold and leaves on its own back at the top: it takes no corner when it is not needed
the platform does the scrolling (scrollTo): smooth, unless less motion is asked for, and then instant
the scroller may not be the document: `scroller` points it at a panel with its own overflow

avoidWhen: the user can remove it or act on it; that is a Tag
it is colored paragraph text; a badge is a capsule, not emphasis
there is no visible text, only a dot; that is BadgeDot
useWhen: a count or a short status attached to something else: unread, quantity, a status label
the tone communicates a system role: success, warning, danger

avoidWhen: there is visible text or a count; that is a Badge
useWhen: a compact dot communicates presence, something new, or a status next to another control

avoidWhen: the badge sits in normal flow; it needs no anchor
useWhen: a Badge or BadgeDot is anchored to the corner of a button or an avatar

avoidWhen: things only need to be spaced apart; that is a Stack, Inline or Grid with no box
a page column needs centering; that is Wrapper
useWhen: a group needs padding, a surface or a border around it

avoidWhen: the navigation is flat; that is a NavList
they are steps of a process; that is Steps
useWhen: the page lives inside a hierarchy and the user needs to go back up it

avoidWhen: it takes the visitor to another page or URL, even if it looks the same: that is Button.navigation
the action is secondary, inside running text: that is a Link
two `solid` + `accent` visible at once: if everything is the main action, nothing is
a tone on a button that acts on nothing: a disclosure or a toggle is neutral, not accent
`danger` on something undone with one click: the tone lies about the cost
`success` or `warning` is wanted: a button performs an action and there is no warning action; a Badge or a Callout reports that
`pressed` on something that does not stay on: a button that fires and springs back is not a toggle, and announcing it as one lies about what it does
`pressed` to mark the chosen item of an exclusive group: that is Segmented or RadioGroup, which also give arrow keys
useWhen: it performs an action in place: it changes something here instead of going somewhere
it submits a form
it confirms or dismisses a dialog
it destroys something or is hard to undo: `tone: danger`, and the emphasis says which of the two moments it is
it is THE action of the view: `tone: accent`, and one per region
a delete inside a row of actions: `variant: ghost` + `tone: danger`, which reads as destructive without becoming the confirm button
the confirm that delete opens: `variant: solid` + `tone: danger`, one per dialog
it sits on media or on a surface of unknown color: `variant: translucent`
the button stays on: `pressed`, a real toggle (bold in a toolbar, a vote, play/pause). Absent when it is not a toggle; `false` when it is one and it is off

avoidWhen: the destination is not available: a link is not disabled, the content is rendered unlinked instead
the link lives inside a paragraph: that is a Link
`tone: danger` on a link: navigating destroys nothing; the destructive part is the action the destination page offers
useWhen: it takes the visitor to another page or URL and has to look like a button
a main call to action that is a link
the same two axes as Button.action: a link can be quiet (`ghost`) and still be the main action (`accent`)

avoidWhen: it is a field inside a form: there the calendar sits behind an input
the date is typed faster than it is found in a grid
useWhen: choosing the date is the screen's task, not one more field of a form
seeing the month helps decide: weekends, holidays, how many days are left
there is room for an always-visible grid

avoidWhen: the message is ephemeral and goes away on its own; that is a Toast
the region is empty for lack of data; that is an EmptyState
useWhen: something that happened has to be told: an error, a confirmation, a warning, or just a side note
the message stays on the page, it does not go away on its own

avoidWhen: the content fits the screen or can reflow without losing meaning: a canvas adds a gesture nobody needed
it is an image that only needs to be seen larger: that is ImageFrame with a link to the full image, or a Dialog with the image
the content is interactive and has to stay usable: drag-to-pan competes with every click and every text selection inside
it is a wide table or list: that is native horizontal scroll inside its own container, which the keyboard and the screen reader already handle
useWhen: a drawing is larger than the screen showing it (a diagram, an anatomy, a plan) and rescaling it beats reflowing it: it is designed at its own width and shown fitted
on a phone the content would be rewrapped word by word: here it is seen whole and small, and the reader zooms into the part they care about
zoom has to feel like a design tool: dragging pans, Ctrl/Cmd + wheel and trackpad pinch zoom around the pointer, `+`/`-`/`0` from the keyboard
it must not hijack the page's scroll: one finger and the plain wheel stay the page's; two fingers and Ctrl + wheel are the canvas's, and a short hint explains it when someone tries the other
an Annotated needs no wrapping: it already brings the same canvas around its frame and keeps the legend outside, unscaled

avoidWhen: the content matters and cannot depend on someone swiping; that is a grid
there are a few items and they all fit; the carousel hides what already fitted
it is a single message rotating on its own; that is little read and much disliked
useWhen: there are many similar items and the horizontal space fits only a few: cards, photos
it should show there is more to the side, with the next item peeking in

avoidWhen: it is outside a Carousel; there is no track to fit into
useWhen: it is one item of the carousel; anything can go inside, usually a card

avoidWhen: they are instructions to read and follow, in order but without versions; that is a ProcessList
what matters is which stage someone is at, what they have done and what is left; that is Steps
it is a single piece of news; one entry with no history around it is not a history
useWhen: there is a version history of something: release notes, a contract's changelog
the reader comes to learn whether they already have the change they are reading, and a version answers that

avoidWhen: outside a Changelog: the rail and the order are drawn by the list, not by a loose release
you want to mark 'unpublished' with a separate option; the missing date already says it, and two fields saying the same thing can contradict each other
useWhen: a version and everything that shipped in it
there is unpublished work: write the version with a -dev suffix and leave the date out

avoidWhen: outside a ChangelogRelease: a change that is not under a version does not say since when it can be relied on
useWhen: one change, with its kind and which part of the contract it touched

avoidWhen: it is ONE measurement within a known range, not a series; that is Meter
it is the progress of a task; that is Progress
the values have to be read precisely, compared row by row or sorted; that is a Table, and a five-bar chart is a worse table
the series has dozens of entries: bars become one-pixel lines and the labels overlap; group the data before drawing it
useWhen: there is a SERIES of named values and its shape needs to be seen: a total per month, per hour, per version
the number of a metric is already stated in text and the chart adds the trend, it does not replace it

avoidWhen: the change takes effect immediately, with nothing to submit; that is a Switch
ONE option of a set is chosen; that is a RadioGroup
useWhen: a yes-or-no decision submitted with the form
several independent options, each checked on its own
accepting terms, subscribing, turning on a preference that is saved on submit

avoidWhen: the options have nothing in common; then they are separate Checkboxes
ONE is chosen; that is a RadioGroup
the parent should be able to stay indeterminate on its own: that state is DERIVED from the children, never chosen
useWhen: a set of options that can also be checked or unchecked as a whole
the selection has to show as partial: some yes, some no
select all in a table, permissions, filters with a master checkbox on top

avoidWhen: whoever copies has to see or check the value first (a share link, a key): that is Clipboard
the action does more than copy (share, export, download): that is a Button with its own name
useWhen: a code block, a command or a token is going to be pasted elsewhere, and selecting it by hand is slow or imprecise
the value is already in view (a code block) or does not need to be seen to be copied

avoidWhen: the value is long or spans several lines (code, configuration): that is a code block with CopyButton
the value can be edited: that is an Input in a FormField
useWhen: the value has to be seen before copying it: a share link, an API key, an identifier
besides the button, the reader may want to select the value or copy it with the keyboard

avoidWhen: it is a literal inside a sentence: that is Code
what matters is copying it, not reading or showing it: that is StateButton composed with the copy behaviour, with no code block around it
useWhen: code has to be shown and should read as code: highlighted, with its label
the block is long and showing it whole pushes the rest of the page out of view

avoidWhen: there is only one version of the code: that is CodePreview and it needs no switch
the two versions are different code, not two levels of detail of the same code
useWhen: the same code has a short version to understand it and a complete one to copy it
showing only the complete one means nobody reads it, and only the short one leaves out what is needed

avoidWhen: the color is always one of a known handful: that is Select or Segmented
space is minimal or the color is secondary to the rest of the form
useWhen: the value is an arbitrary color, not one of a few fixed options
the hue, saturation and transparency should be seen and adjusted by hand

avoidWhen: an exact value has to be typed (hex, RGB, HSL or OKLCH): that is ColorPicker
useWhen: the swatch lives in a toolbar or another tight place
the reader only needs the area, the hue and presets, not every channel separately

avoidWhen: OKLCH, presets or seeing the channels while adjusting are needed: that is ColorPicker
useWhen: an ordinary color inside a form, with no presets or channels of its own
the operating system's picker and the submission should belong to the browser

avoidWhen: the options fit in view: a select already handles choosing from a known list
the value is free and does not come from a list: that is an input with suggestions
useWhen: the list is long: typing to filter gets there before scanning it
each option needs a description under its label, not only text
several have to be chosen and seen as removable chips

avoidWhen: the options are few and fit in view: that is a Menu
it is the only way to reach something: a palette complements navigation, it does not replace it
a form field that filters a known list is needed: that is a Combobox
useWhen: there are many destinations or actions and typing the name gets there before browsing them
frequent users of the product want to get there without navigating

avoidWhen: the stream is flat, with no nested replies; that is a Feed
it is a selectable hierarchy (files, an index); that is a TreeView
there is one comment and nothing around it; that is a single Comment
useWhen: there is a conversation with nested replies and it needs a container that names it

avoidWhen: it is content of a flat stream with no replies; that is a FeedArticle
useWhen: one unit of conversation: who wrote it, when, and what it said
a comment has to be quoted outside its thread; it needs no container

avoidWhen: the comment is read-only; then this is simply not composed
it is an action bar for a whole view, not for one unit of content; that is a Toolbar
useWhen: a comment takes actions: vote, reply, delete

avoidWhen: it is a single rating with no direction (a like); that is a StateButton
useWhen: there is a score that goes up or down, with the reader's own vote reflected

the product reacts rather than ranks, with like and dislike instead of upvote and downvote: `voteStyle: "like"` draws thumbs, and both labels are then passed (`Like`, `Dislike`, or the product's own words)

avoidWhen: the markup is re-rendered whole; in React it is not needed, it simply renders again
what is created is a transient notice and not a comment; that is a ToastTemplate
useWhen: the app creates comments at runtime and needs a blueprint to clone

avoidWhen: the form does more than publish a body of text; that is a form of its own with FormField
useWhen: a comment or a reply has to be written, with whatever control the consumer decides

avoidWhen: Vanilla and React of the SAME component have to be compared: that is this site's machinery, not a published contract
the block is only code, with nothing to show above it: that is CodePreview alone
useWhen: something has to be shown next to its source code: an example, a demo, a use case
the docs surface does not need to compare two bindings or screen presets

avoidWhen: there is a single message and it is part of the page; that is a Callout in place
useWhen: the page is going to show toasts: they belong to it, and without a region there is nowhere to put them
they have to announce themselves; the region is what the screen reader is already watching

avoidWhen: the Toast already exists in the region from the first render
useWhen: a script is going to clone the same Toast anatomy for dynamic messages

avoidWhen: the message is part of the content and has to stay; that is a Callout
it must be read before going on; that is a Dialog
it is an error of one field; that goes in the FormField, next to the control
useWhen: confirming something that already happened and needs no answer: saved, sent, copied
offering to undo an action for a few seconds
saying that something running in the background has finished

avoidWhen: choosing the date IS the screen: there the grid is always visible
only the month or the year matters, not the day
useWhen: the date is a field of a form, next to other fields
it should be possible both to type it and to look it up in the calendar

avoidWhen: a range is needed (start and end): that is DatePicker with selectionMode range
the calendar has to be always visible: that is Calendar
useWhen: an ordinary date inside a form, with no range selection
the keyboard, the local format and the submission should belong to the browser

avoidWhen: the same fields are shown for SEVERAL records; a cell that means something because of its row and its column is a Table
the pairs are form controls a person fills in; that is FormField
it is a list of things rather than of facts about one thing; that is List
useWhen: the details of ONE record are shown as name and value: a summary, metadata, specs, key facts
each row is a complete statement on its own and nothing is compared across rows
the names are short and repeat the same shape: Status, Placed, Total, Tracking

avoidWhen: the name needs markup of its own; a name that is a heading means this should be a section
useWhen: one name and its value; the name is text, the value takes markup (a Tag, a link, a date)

avoidWhen: what has to be named are the parts of one thing already drawn: that is Annotation, which anchors each label to a selector inside the subject and does not draw a graph

the content is a sequence with no branches and no loops: that is ProcessList if they are instructions, or Steps if progress is primary; a single-column diagram with no forks is a list with extra lines
the hierarchy is containment and not flow (folders, a file tree): that is TreeView or Folder, where what matters is what is inside what

the graph is large, comes from data, or has to be explored or have its nodes dragged: this does not do layout, it draws small hand-written diagrams. Wrapping it in a Canvas is enough to zoom and pan the view

full UML notation, swimlanes or box types by convention (cylinder, parallelogram, hexagon) are needed: those are conventions the reader has to be taught, and of the prose shapes only the three understood without a legend live here. Logic gates are the exception and pass the same test from the other side: they are not a box that means AND, they are the symbol the standard assigns to conjunction, and anyone who reads the notation reads it without a legend

a real schematic is needed: this draws the seven gates and nothing else. There are no flip-flops, buses, multiplexers, components with numbered pins, junction nodes or netlist; a gate holds nothing inside either, so a visible designator (`U1`) has nowhere to go

the logic drawing needs feedback: a latch of cross-coupled gates cannot be drawn here. Operands have to come from earlier columns, which is the order a schematic is drawn in anyway; a wire going backwards bends halfway between its two ends, and if both gates share a column that point falls inside both and the wire runs under the symbol it was feeding
useWhen: how several things relate has to be explained: a linear flow, an if/else, a decision tree, a state machine with a loop. All four come from the same two pieces, they are not four modes

the boxes are ordinary HTML content and the drawing is everything else: the runtime measures and computes the routes, the elbows, the arrowheads and where each label lands. Whoever composes never writes a coordinate

the layout is an ordinary CSS grid: `columns` on the frame and `span` on a node cover the usual shapes, and anything else is `grid-area` in the consumer's own stylesheet. If a media query moves a node, the connectors redraw themselves
the relationship has to reach a screen reader: the SVG is `aria-hidden` and the binding writes an announced list of where it leads inside each node, so the drawing can be read without seeing it
a loop is needed: an edge to a node higher up leaves through the margin and comes back, which is how "and start again" has always been drawn
the edges are not a sequence but a relation between things (a model, a schema): `arrow: "none"` draws the line with no head and the label carries the cardinality
a node has to say more than one line of text: its slot takes a composition, so any tree of the catalogue fits inside

what has to be drawn is boolean logic: `shape` brings the seven gates of IEEE 91 / IEC 60617-12 notation (`and`, `or`, `xor`, `nand`, `nor`, `xnor`, `not`), with the real shape and not a box that says AND inside

the diagram is wider than the screen showing it (four columns on a phone): wrapped in a `Canvas` it is designed at its desktop width and shown fitted, with zoom, instead of squeezing each box to one word per line
a gate and a step go in the same drawing: they are one `Diagram`, so a gate's result can feed a process box and a step's output can be an operand, without switching components halfway

avoidWhen: it is auxiliary information that does not block; that is a Tooltip or a Popover
it is a list of actions hanging from a button; that is a Menu
the content is long or navigable: that needs a page, not a modal box
the panel has to take a whole edge at full height: that is Vaul.drawer
useWhen: something has to be decided before going on: confirming a deletion, completing a short step
the footer's action row should sit at the start or the end of the inline axis (`footerAlign`; the end by default)
the rest of the page should be inert meanwhile
on mobile the same dialog can be asked for as a sheet from the bottom (the vaul option)
a destructive confirmation or a blocking error that needs immediate attention (the alert option)

avoidWhen: the field is a single line, or needs no formatting at all: Input/Textarea is enough there
useWhen: styled text is needed - bold, lists, headings, quotes - not only plain text
the formatting toolbar should come ready, without composing it by hand

avoidWhen: the data is loading; that is a Loader or a Placeholder
there was an error; there the message is a Callout, not an empty state
useWhen: a list or a region has nothing to show, and why has to be said
it is the first time and the action that fills it should be offered

avoidWhen: the content is not clipped; fading it only lowers contrast
the gradient protects text over a photo; that is MediaGradient inside MediaCaption
the fade would hide a control or information needed at rest
the clipped edge is a Marquee's viewport; Marquee already has its own inner fade, and a FadeEdge around it also washes out the Play/Pause
useWhen: a clipped edge needs to show visually that the content continues, or enters and leaves the surface
the effect has to wrap another component without changing its semantics, focus or behaviour

avoidWhen: it is a list of options to choose from; that is a Listbox or a List
the order matters by fixed position, not by publication; that is a Table or a plain List
the conversation has nested replies and actions (vote, reply); that is a CommentThread
there are no posts yet and the message is the absence itself; that is an EmptyState
useWhen: a stream of independent units of content that can load in batches. Posts, comments, activity

avoidWhen: the comment takes nested replies or actions; that is a Comment inside a CommentThread
useWhen: one unit of content inside the feed. A post, a comment

avoidWhen: it is a single profile photo cropped right there; that needs its own flow
the value is text, even if it comes from a file; that is an Input or a Textarea
the control needs the form's own hint and error around it; that is FormField around it
useWhen: files have to be attached: a resume, a receipt, photos
drag and drop should be accepted besides the button, without forcing anyone to drag
dropping the file on a whole panel or the whole page is expected, not only on the dashed box; that is dropScope element or page, with overlayLabel so the target shows

avoidWhen: it is a surface with no label of its own; that is a Box, which draws nothing
the whole surface is a control; that is a TileLink or a TileButton, which already bring a control's state and focus
the content opens and closes; that is an Accordion or a Details
useWhen: a block of content needs to say what it is about BEFORE it is read: the tab is a label, not one more heading
there is a collection of things of the same kind and each should read as a separate object
at rest it should read as clean text: a folder is never seen until it is touched

avoidWhen: the folder does something on the page instead of navigating; that is a TileButton
there is more than one destination inside; nested links do not exist, put the links in the body of a Folder
useWhen: the whole folder goes somewhere: the complete rectangle is the destination
the reveal has to respond to the keyboard without depending on what is inside

avoidWhen: the image is the folder's content and not a preview; that goes in the body, where it can be reached
it is outside a Folder: alone it means nothing
useWhen: it goes in the previews slot of a Folder or a FolderLink: it is the box of ONE image of the fan
the image needs its own mat and shadow, which the image alone cannot carry

avoidWhen: each folder needs to be seen whole; that is a Grid or an Inline of Folders
the set is a list with semantics of its own (results, steps); whoever contains it names that, not this
useWhen: the folders read as a stack: each shows its tab and a strip of body
the overlap itself is the information, that there is more below and there is an order

avoidWhen: a section only needs separating from the rest with padding or a border mid-page; that is a Box
it is an action bar stuck to the bottom of a panel or a dialog (a row of confirm buttons); that is composed with layout.Inline inside the container, not with Footer
each column of links would have no accessible name: an unnamed navigation in the landmark list is worse than none; each column is a NavList with an aria-label or a visible heading
the footer needs more than two hierarchy levels competing (columns, newsletter band, legal bar, sub-credit, all at once with no order): move what is extra into its own region before the footer
useWhen: it closes the page: the final band that says "the page ends here", with secondary navigation, legal notice or credit
the host is a document-level <footer>, which IS the contentinfo landmark without writing a role: never put role="contentinfo" by hand
there is at most ONE document <footer> per page; a footer that truly belongs to an <article> is valid but stops being the landmark, and that is the composer's decision

the anatomy is free, like Hero's: inside, compose with layout.Grid for the row of columns, nav-list.NavList for each column (with its own accessible name), typography.Text for the legal notice, wrapper.Wrapper to hold the page's measure
by default surface="sunken" and divider (a top border) on: a footer sharing the page's background reads as "more content", which is the one thing a footer is not

avoidWhen: the control carries no label at all; then the control itself carries aria-label and there is no FormField (labelHidden is NOT this: the slot is still required)
the aim is to mark it invalid without saying why; the error's presence is what invalidates, and color is never the only signal
the control already brings its own label wired by its machine, like NumberField or Combobox; wrapping it would add a second `for` competing with the first
useWhen: a control needs a label, and it almost always does
a validation message has to be shown next to the control
a short hint is needed before the user types
the label has to exist for the screen reader but the composition already says it visually: labelHidden clips it without dropping the for

avoidWhen: it is one more section of the page, not the opening one; that is a Box or simply a Stack
content only needs separating with padding or a border; that is a Box
the message needs more than two actions or more than one competing headline; move the rest into its own section
an image inside replaces the headline instead of accompanying it; the headline stays a real Heading, and the image carries its own alt
it closes the page (secondary navigation, legal notice, credit); that is Footer
useWhen: it opens a page or a section: it needs to stand apart visually from what follows
the headline and the sub-line need more room and a surface of their own, not the page's background
a real heading (Heading) always goes inside, never just large text: if the hero opens the whole page, that heading is the page's <h1>
at most one primary action and one quieter secondary one; never a row of buttons of equal weight
the default host is not a landmark and needs no aria-label; authored as a landmark (<section>, as="section" in React) it does need aria-label or aria-labelledby pointing at the heading inside

avoidWhen: it is a product concept (an invoice, an airplane): that is passed as icon data in the React binding, not as a stable name
it would get a label inside a button that already has text; the accessible name would be duplicated
a button-shaped control is needed: that is Button (iconOnly) or StateButton, not an Icon alone
useWhen: it reinforces an action that already has text; without a label, decorative
it is the only content of a square control, and then the CONTROL carries the accessible name, not the icon
the name is a role the system names: delete, visibility, chevron-down

avoidWhen: it is a person's round identity: that is an Avatar
there is no media to show, neither src nor authored content; an empty frame is an empty box, not a placeholder
the content has not loaded yet and a silhouette is needed: that is Placeholder, not an ImageFrame with no src
useWhen: it crops an image or a video to a fixed aspect ratio
the photo has to fill a box without distorting
which part of the image survives the crop has to be decided

avoidWhen: the text is long or multi-line; that is Textarea
validity depends on the server (a RUT that is already registered); that is FormField's `error` slot, written by the composer, and it wins over the `format` message
a phone number should be validated without adding dependencies: there is no way; the numbering plan is data and the kit prefers not validating to validating wrongly
the value is chosen from a closed set of options; that is a Select
the value is a number with a step and bounds; that is NumberField
the platform should govern time/color/range and its native control is wanted; that is NativeInput

useWhen: the enhancer has to generate a TablePager's page controls

avoidWhen: each section's content is long and the user would want to see it all together: that is an Accordion or a page with sections
each tab navigates to another URL: that is a NavList
there is a single section; a lone tab is not a choice
useWhen: several sections share one region and only one is seen at a time
the content is siblings, not a hierarchy: every tab is at the same level
the user switches between views of the same object (summary, activity, settings)
the list always carries a name (aria-label, or aria-labelledby pointing at a visible title)

avoidWhen: it is only a count or a system status nobody can touch; that is a Badge
useWhen: a label that classifies content: an applied filter, a facet, a keyword
the user can remove it (removable), or it only names a topic in a list

avoidWhen: it also has to be removable; a link tag is not dismissible because it cannot contain another button
it is a link inside a sentence; that is Link
useWhen: a label that navigates to a facet, a topic or a keyword

avoidWhen: the values must come from a known list; that is a Combobox, and choosing this instead means accepting typos as data
there is one value; that is an Input
the chips are not a field at all but applied filters or keywords to display; that is Tag
what is being added comes from the platform rather than the keyboard; that is FileUpload
useWhen: several values are typed into one field: keywords, recipients, labels, skills
the vocabulary is the person's own, so whatever they type is a valid value
the values are short enough to read as chips; a long phrase in a chip is a truncation

avoidWhen: there is more than one action inside; two nested targets are a trap, not a card
it navigates nowhere; that is a TileButton
useWhen: the whole card goes to the same place and the whole of it should be clickable
a grid of destinations: projects, articles, sections

avoidWhen: the action is choosing among several and the choice shows; that is TileCheckbox or a RadioGroup
it navigates; that is a TileLink
useWhen: the whole card triggers an action: choosing a plan, starting a flow

avoidWhen: it is outside a Tile; it is not standalone content
useWhen: a Tile needs the shared anatomy of title and description

avoidWhen: it is outside an expandable trigger: it is not a general-purpose icon
the state needs announcing; the trigger's aria-expanded already says it
useWhen: an expandable tile or an accordion section needs to show that it opens and closes

avoidWhen: it is a single option in a text list; that is a Checkbox
only one can be chosen; that is a TileRadioGroup
useWhen: several options are chosen and each is a card with content of its own
the whole card should be the click target, not only the little box

avoidWhen: the change only applies when the form is submitted; there a Checkbox tells the truth
it is one option among several; that is a TileRadioGroup
useWhen: the card turns something on or off and the effect is immediate: a preference, an integration

avoidWhen: the options are one word each; that is a RadioGroup or a Segmented
several can be chosen; that is TileCheckbox
useWhen: a single option is chosen and each one needs explaining: plans, shipping methods
the options are best compared side by side before deciding

avoidWhen: the content is what the person came to read; hiding it adds a click and nothing else
it floats over the page; that is a Popover or a Dialog
useWhen: there is detail not everyone needs, and hiding it lowers the page's noise
there are several sections and only one matters at a time; there an Accordion is built from these

avoidWhen: it is outside an ExpandableTile; it has nothing to point at
useWhen: it is the header that opens and closes its ExpandableTile

avoidWhen: it is outside an ExpandableTile; nothing opens it
useWhen: it is the body that folds inside its ExpandableTile

avoidWhen: the day is needed too; that is a DatePicker, or both together
it is a duration, not a time of day; that is a NumberField with its unit
useWhen: a time has to be typed and the format matters: a booking, a shift, opening hours
each segment should be correctable separately without retyping everything
the format has to follow the locale (12 or 24 hours, AM/PM before or after)

avoidWhen: the reader is inside the process and has to be told which stage they are at; that is Steps
they are instructions to follow, with no time at all; that is a ProcessList
they are shipped releases; that is Changelog, which has its own vocabulary and scale
useWhen: events that already happened have to be shown, in the order they happened
the when matters as much as the what: a history, order tracking, an activity log
the author sets the direction by writing the entries in it; there is no order option

avoidWhen: the event carries complete / current / upcoming; that is a step of Steps
useWhen: one event on the rail: a required heading, and optionally a time, an icon and a detail
the time is two fields: time (ISO, for the machine) and timeLabel (the visible copy)
tone marks the dot a scanning eye should stop at; it is never the only thing saying so

avoidWhen: the destinations are different pages, not sections of THIS page: that is NavList
the document is short and fits on one screen: an index saves nothing there
useWhen: a long document has several sections (h2/h3) and the reader needs to jump between them
which section is being read has to be visible while reading: the scroll-spy moves the "current"
the title names the nav and heads the list, so it is always there ("On this page")

avoidWhen: they are two or three loose buttons; an Inline is enough there
the controls are the site's navigation links; that is NavList or Navbar, not a toolbar
useWhen: there are many controls together and the keyboard should not pay one stop for each
a Segmented or Tabs can go inside: the bar counts each as a single stop
a subset of controls that belong together; with groupLabel when the bar has more than one kind of group
two groups have to be separated visually

avoidWhen: the text is the only name or the only information available; it has to live outside the tooltip
the content needs actions, formatting or several lines; use Popover
it is a list of actions; that is a Menu
useWhen: a control already has an accessible name and needs a short description on hover or focus
an icon-only button needs a redundant visual hint for whoever can see it

avoidWhen: the explanation is about a single control and is needed on hover or focus: that is Tooltip
steps that change data have to be completed (a sign-up, a configuration): that is a multi-step form with Steps, not a tour that points
the content is long or needs images and examples: that is a help page or a Dialog, not a box next to an element
the feature can only be understood with the tour: if a piece needs a tour to be used, the problem is the piece
useWhen: a new or redesigned interface has a few pieces worth pointing out in order (three to five), and its user can ask for the tour whenever they want
each step fits in one idea: what this element is and what it is for, in one or two sentences
the page has to stay usable during the tour: no backdrop covering it, no blocked clicks and no trapped focus

avoidWhen: the tour should start on its own when the page loads: a tour never starts without someone asking for it
useWhen: the tour has to be startable, and repeatable after skipping or finishing it, from a visible and stable place (help, the header)

avoidWhen: there is a single level; that is a List or a NavList
there are two fixed, known levels; a NavList with groups reads better
each hierarchical row also has columns (size, date, owner); that is a Treegrid
they are links to navigate the site or the page; a role=tree is not navigation: that is NavList or Toc
useWhen: the data truly nests and the hierarchy is part of what has to be understood
branches have to open and close without losing sight of where you are
a file explorer, an org chart, categories to choose from
almost always: the same reason as TableScroll. The grid must not break a flex or a grid by being wider than its space

avoidWhen: there are columns but no hierarchy; that is a Table
there is hierarchy but a single text column; that is a TreeView
useWhen: the data has hierarchy AND columns at once. A file explorer with size/date, an org chart with role/department
each row needs to expand or collapse without losing the rest of its columns
the columns have headers, which is almost always
whenever there is a TreegridHead: it is the row holding the TreegridColumnHeaders
the cell names its column
always: it is where the grid's rows live, and the grid is not complete without it

avoidWhen: the row is a leaf with no children; there `expanded` is not passed at all. Its absence is what marks it a leaf, not a `false` value
useWhen: one record of the grid, in the same order a screen reader walks it: never nested inside another TreegridRow, a <tr> cannot contain another <tr>
the row has descendants: pass `expanded` (true or false) and write them right after, in order, with a higher `level`
every row carries a `value` unique in the grid: it is what the expand and activate events report

avoidWhen: the content needs its own interactive control (a button, a link); this version of the contract is faithful to the WAI `treegrid-1` example. Text-only cells, see docs/aria-apg-audit.md
useWhen: a value inside a row of the grid

avoidWhen: it titles a section; that is a Heading, even if it looks small

it goes inside another line of text, a button or a label as a

: there it is textElement span
useWhen: a paragraph, a sub-line, a footnote
the tone says hierarchy: secondary for what is accessory, danger for an error in prose (with text that says so, not only the color)
the small line above a title is textRole eyebrow; the sub-line under the title is textRole subtitle

avoidWhen: it titles a section; that is a Heading
only a different weight for the whole line is wanted, without saying it matters more; that is Text with weight
useWhen: a phrase inside text has strong importance, not just a different visual weight

avoidWhen: it is static text unrelated to any computation; that is Text
useWhen: it shows the computed result of an input or an interaction; outputFor names the ids of those inputs

avoidWhen: it is a whole block of code: that is CodePreview, with its scroll and its copy button
only emphasis is wanted; that is Strong, and it is a different claim
useWhen: there is a literal inside a sentence: a path, a flag, a property name
it should read differently from the surrounding text so it is not mistaken for prose

avoidWhen: only large text is wanted; the level is structure, not size
the title is a group's small label (a kicker); that is Text with textRole eyebrow
useWhen: it opens a section and which document level it belongs to has to be said: headingElement (h1–h6) is the level, headingSize only the look
the size is chosen by step (h1–h6, display-sm/md/lg); sm, md, lg and display are legacy aliases

avoidWhen: it looks and works like a button; that is Button.navigation
useWhen: a link inside a sentence, underlined and in the flow of the text

avoidWhen: it is a short decision that has to be confirmed: that is Dialog, centered and with a title of its own
it is a Dialog that should become a bottom sheet only on mobile: that is Dialog with vaul, which keeps its header and its title
it does not block the rest of the screen: that is Popover
useWhen: a modal panel arrives from an edge and can be closed by dragging it: a filter, an action sheet, sharing
on mobile the task should rest on an edge rather than in a centered box

avoidWhen: a sheet resting on the edge is enough: that is Vaul
the navigation has to stay visible beside the content: a drawer is modal and blocks the page; that is Sidebar
useWhen: the modal panel takes its whole edge: mobile navigation, a side panel of filters
the content is a long list that needs the full height

avoidWhen: the panel opens from script, not from a button; then no trigger is needed
it opens a popover or a menu anchored to the button; that is Popover or Menu, which bring their own trigger
useWhen: a button on the page opens a Vaul: opens is the panel's panelId, and both go in the same tree

avoidWhen: the button confirms an action besides closing; there a Button that performs the action and closes from its own handler fits better
useWhen: the panel needs a button of its own to close (a Done, an X): it goes inside the Vaul

avoidWhen: something has to be decided before going on; that is a Dialog, which makes the page inert
the content hangs from a control and closes on an outside click; that is a Popover
the panel comes in from an edge and does not move; that is a Vaul
the content has to stay visible without JavaScript: a window does not open without its machine
useWhen: a panel has to live alongside the page: a tool palette, an inspector, a chat that stays open beside the work
whoever uses it has to be able to move it, resize it or minimize it to see what it covers

avoidWhen: the content should touch the edges (a full-bleed image or band); full still leaves gutters, so there is no wrapper there, or LayoutGrid with data-width="full-width" is used
some children should be narrower or wider than the rest; that is LayoutGrid, not nested Wrappers
it is already inside another Wrapper; nesting them adds both inline paddings and the outer ceiling wins anyway
the region needs a background, border or padding of its own; Wrapper only measures and centers, that is a Box (inside or outside the Wrapper)
useWhen: the page needs a centered measure so the text does not stretch edge to edge
a header, a body and a footer should share the same width ceiling: all three use the same wrapperSize
the content needs side gutters but no ceiling; that is wrapperSize full, which keeps the inline padding and only drops the maximum
